title: Add support for HTML rich text in Calendar Events in Calendar widget
line: Calendar event titles with formatting now show bold, italic and colored text in the Digital Clock's event list instead of raw HTML tags.
explanation: Some calendars (like the reporter's liturgical calendar .ics) store HTML formatting in the event summary. The Digital Clock agenda forced the title label to plain text, so the tags were printed literally, while the event description right below it already detects rich text. The change drops the plain-text override on the title so it auto-detects rich text like the description, and opens links in titles like the description does.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: show rich text in event titles

Event titles were always shown as plain text, so calendars that store
formatting in the summary showed raw HTML tags in the agenda. Let the
title detect rich text like the description below it already does.

BUG: 520844

From da2b9827fd133ef21e90800ab2173237ee584ddf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 19:54:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/digital-clock: show rich text in event titles

Event titles were always shown as plain text, so calendars that store
formatting in the summary showed raw HTML tags in the agenda. Let the
title detect rich text like the description below it already does.

BUG: 520844
---
 applets/digital-clock/CalendarView.qml | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/digital-clock/CalendarView.qml b/applets/digital-clock/CalendarView.qml
index 48d5dcccb7..bdb9f58bfa 100644
--- a/applets/digital-clock/CalendarView.qml
+++ b/applets/digital-clock/CalendarView.qml
@@ -350,9 +350,10 @@ PlasmaExtras.Representation {
                                 Layout.fillWidth: true
 
                                 text: eventItem.modelData.title
-                                textFormat: Text.PlainText
                                 verticalAlignment: Text.AlignVCenter
                                 wrapMode: Text.Wrap
+
+                                onLinkActivated: link => Qt.openUrlExternally(link)
                             }
 
                             Kirigami.SelectableLabel {
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Events with HTML titles from the reporter's .ics show raw tags in the agenda
Same events with the fix: bold, colored and italic text; the plain title with < and & is unchanged

review.text: Dropping `textFormat: Text.PlainText` on `eventTitle` in `CalendarView.qml` makes `Kirigami.SelectableLabel` fall back to `TextEdit.AutoText` (full `QTextDocument` `RichText`) and activates `Qt.openUrlExternally` on links inside event titles. Per RFC 5545, iCalendar `SUMMARY` is plain text (which is why Thunderbird and KOrganizer intentionally display raw HTML for that malformed `.ics`), and auto-detecting arbitrary HTML on untrusted event titles breaks legitimate plain-text titles containing HTML-like tags (e.g. `<div>`, `<b>`), introduces HTML/link-spoofing and layout-injection risks from external invites, renders hardcoded colors (like `maroon`/`blue`) illegibly on dark themes, and still leaks raw HTML tags into `eventItem.text` for screen readers. This is a bad security and correctness trade-off and should not be merged as-is.
changes: Do not switch `eventTitle` to unrestricted `TextEdit.AutoText` with `Qt.openUrlExternally` on plain-text iCalendar summaries.

If rich-text event summaries are explicitly wanted by Plasma/VDG, plumb an explicit rich-text flag from calendar plugins (e.g. `KCalendarCore::Incidence::summaryIsRich()`), sanitize/restrict allowed markup (e.g. basic inline styling without arbitrary links or hardcoded unreadable colors), and pass plain stripped text to `eventItem.text` / `Accessible.name`.
